request.system: You are an experiment designer for a fraud ranking model. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Propose 3 or 4 distinct configurations to test next with 5-fold cross-validation. Each must differ meaningfully (model family, feature set, imbalance handling or capacity). You only see cross-validation results; the test set is hidden from you. You can preview a configuration on 3 CV folds before including it in your batch. Use the preview to filter out bad configs and only propose ones that show promise. (Independent run 1.)

proposals.rationale: Best preview: PR-AUC 0.7152 (sd 0.071) and precision@50 0.773 on 3 folds. Fold SD is large, so this is a promising lead and not a confirmed winner. Without imbalance handling it should keep probabilities well ranked for a top-100 audit queue. Previewed with learning_rate 0.05 and num_leaves 15.

Preview PR-AUC 0.6814 with precision@50 of 0.76, close to the best on top-of-queue precision. It tests whether dropping size features and adding agent features reduces reliance on provider volume. That matters because the label may reflect suspicion that correlates with size. Previewed with learning_rate 0.05 and num_leaves 7.

A different model family: PR-AUC 0.6635 and precision@50 0.733 in preview. It is a lower-variance bagged baseline that is less prone to overfitting a noisy, undocumented label. Previewed with 500 trees, min_samples_leaf 3.
A linear baseline with the lowest fold SD (0.04) and PR-AUC 0.6558 in preview. It is a useful interpretable check on whether the tree models' gains are real, and it is a stable comparison point.
